source.author: verg
source.text: Non alios prima crescentis origine mundi illuxisse dies aliumve habuisse tenorem crediderim: ver illud erat, ver magnus agebat orbis et hibernis parcebant flatibus Euri, cum primae lucem pecudes hausere virumque terrea progenies duris caput extulit arvis, immissaeque ferae silvis et sidera caelo.
source.text_original: Non alios prima crescentis origine mundi / illuxisse dies aliumve habuisse tenorem / crediderim: ver illud erat, ver magnus agebat / orbis et hibernis parcebant flatibus Euri, / cum primae lucem pecudes hausere virumque / terrea progenies duris caput extulit arvis, / immissaeque ferae silvis et sidera caelo.
source.text_english: I would not believe that any other days dawned at the very beginning of the growing world, or that it had any different aspect: that was spring, spring the great world was passing through, and the East Winds were sparing their wintry blasts, when the flocks first drew in light and the earth-born race raised its head from the hard fields, and wild beasts were loosed into the woods, and stars into the sky.

reuse.author: lact
reuse.text: unde illud est Vergilianum uirumque terrea progenies duris caput extulit aruis.
reuse.text_original: unde illud est Vergilianum uirumque terrea progenies duris caput extulit aruis.
reuse.text_english: Hence that Virgilian line, and man, the offspring of the earth, raised his head from the stubborn fields.
